title: Parashurama's challenge
hook: Rama strings the bow, and then has to decide where the arrow goes
carry: leave me my power to move

segments.voice: Yesterday: an axe on his shoulder, Vishnu's bow in his hand, and a dare for a young prince. Your line was string this one, then we fight.

The king has begged and been ignored. The whole wedding party stands frozen on the road, the brides in their carriages, the soldiers with their hands near their swords. Every eye is on one young man, just married, who has been told to string a god's bow and then fight a warrior who has made kings tremble. You might expect a duel. Valmiki doesn't write one. What Rama does next is quick and quiet, and it ends with nobody hurt.
screen: `THE ROAD STANDS FROZEN.` → `A DUEL? NO.` → `QUICK, QUIET, NOBODY HURT.`

segments.voice: Rama speaks politely and firmly. He has heard what Parashurama did to avenge his father, he says, and he respects it. But you've taken me for someone weak. Watch. He takes the bow out of the sage's hands, strings it, and fits an arrow. Then the surprise. You're a brahmin, Rama says, and related to my teacher Vishvamitra, so I won't loose this at you. But a drawn arrow can't go to waste. It will destroy one of two things: your power to move freely through the world, or the worlds of merit you've won by your austerities. You choose. The gods, the text says, gather in the sky to watch. And the fire goes out of Parashurama. I gave the whole earth away to the sage Kashyapa, he says, and promised not to stay on it at night. Leave me my power to move. Take the worlds I've won. Rama looses the arrow, and those worlds are gone. Then the older warrior says he knows who stands before him: the undying Lord, the slayer of the demon Madhu. He walks around Rama with respect and leaves for the Mahendra mountain. Rama hands Vishnu's bow to Varuna, god of the waters, for keeping, and the family rides into Ayodhya to music and banners. Valmiki closes his first book gently. Bharata goes to visit his mother's family in the kingdom of Kekaya, and Shatrughna goes with him. Rama stays home, and he and Sita grow in love, the text says, each living in the other's heart. Remember that Bharata is far away. It matters very soon.
screen: `RAMA STRINGS THE BOW.` · `ONE ARROW, TWO CHOICES.` · `PARASHURAMA GIVES UP HIS WORLDS.` · `THE FIRST BOOK CLOSES AT HOME.` · then, large: `BHARATA IS FAR AWAY.`

segments.voice: Picture Rama on that road: the bow strung, the arrow ready, and a choice not to point it at the person in front of him. Breathe in and feel the strength you actually have; breathe out and feel how much of it you don't need to use.
Parashurama's challenge, answered. Rama strings Vishnu's bow, spares the sage, and takes only the worlds he had won by austerity.
Your line: leave me my power to move. Rama won without aiming at anyone. Day five hundred thirteen, and the first book is done.

howItsDone: In devotional readings this episode is heard as one avatar of Vishnu meeting the next, and the Bala Kanda as the happy prelude before the Ayodhya Kanda's exile.

fork.setup: you're Rama, holding a strung bow and an arrow that can't go to waste. what do you aim at?
options: the worlds of merit the sage has won.
fork.reveal: Rama spares the man and lets him choose: his free movement or his merit-worlds. Parashurama gives up the worlds.

original.note: Sanskrit dhanus: bow. two great bows, Shiva's broken at Mithila and Vishnu's strung on the road, close the first book.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama defeats Parashurama in a great battle.
what it means: there's no fight; Rama strings the bow and spares him.

what a scholar hears: some scholars treat the Bala Kanda as a later layer of the epic, and see scenes like this one, where an avatar meets an avatar, as part of how Rama's divinity was drawn into the story.

chat.says: In Valmiki, Rama strings the bow and draws an arrow. Who does he shoot?
options: No one. He spares the sage, and the arrow takes only the worlds he'd won.
Parashurama himself, who falls wounded on the road and then flees.
A tree by the road, to show the whole wedding party his aim.
chat.meaning: Rama won't loose it at a brahmin kin to his teacher. Parashurama chooses: leave me my power to move, take the worlds I've won.
